paper.title: The SKINNY Family of Block Ciphers and its Low-Latency Variant MANTIS

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm description; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: SKINNY-128-256 (48 rounds) and SKINNY-128-384 (56 rounds) encrypt the plaintexts of Appendix B of the SKINNY-AEAD specification to the printed ciphertexts (2 of 2)
SKINNY-128-384+ (the 40-round variant used by Romulus) encrypts the Romulus specification's test plaintext to its printed ciphertext (1 of 1)
the 8-bit S-box rebuilt from its NOR/XOR bit-level description equals the Appendix A table (256 of 256)

expected_values_source.what: Appendices A and B of the SKINNY-AEAD and SKINNY-Hash round-2 specification document (by the SKINNY designers), and the Skinny-128-384+ test vector of the Romulus final-round specification, parsed from the PDF text by a script
expected_values_source.note: the algorithm is the one in section 2.3 of the SKINNY-AEAD document, not the CRYPTO 2016 paper (not fetched). The text extraction of that document dropped the overbar of the NOR in the S-box formula; the document itself calls the construction NOR/XOR, and the NOR form reproduces all 256 table entries. The 40-round Skinny-128-384+ vector belongs to the Romulus document, not to the SKINNY paper. Data copied as numbers; no code was copied

negative_control: built with SKINNY_LFSR_TK2_TAP=4 (wrong tap in the TK2 LFSR), 0 of 3 vectors match and the program exits 1 (the S-box check still passes, 256 of 256)
not_checked: the SKINNY-64 variants and SKINNY-128-128 (no vectors fetched)
the tweakable-block-cipher security claims, the AEAD and hash modes
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces three published SKINNY ciphertexts and the full published S-box. Three vectors are a thin test; it does not show SKINNY is secure.
